reviews.comment: The book is on the table, but don't let that deceive you. There is a nonzero change that it will fall through the table

reviews.comment: Teizer loves what he teaches and his accent is great. However, he is also unfortunately teaching one of the hardest subjects most engineers will ever take and he does not grade easy. Great guy, but you will suffer.

reviews.comment: Honestly not as awful as people say he is. It's a class that requires a lot of work but as long as you have time you will do decently well. reviews.comment: He lectures well but his homeworks and exams are extremely difficult. Provided formula chart is insufficient. Take this class with an easier professor. Cool guy though.

reviews.comment: His lectures do not include any example problems, which make up the bulk of the homework and tests.  However, the exams were not that bad (questions are mostly plug-n-chug). My advice is to familiarize yourself with his formula sheet and learn how to use each formula. Use the textbook for example problems and for learning how to use each formula.

reviews.comment: This is not the guy to take for 222. Push back to avoid him. Teaches the lectures like a history class (no examples and constantly going off on tangents). reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Obviously passionate about the material and has some interesting lectures but really only discusses theory during class while the homework is mostly quantitative. Tests form the majority of your grade and are very difficult while he never gives a good layout on what will be on the exams and provides poor formula sheets before the exam date.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is one of the worst in the department, not only are his lectures terrible but he doesn't even care to give a formula sheet that is formatted clear and understandable for exams. On the first exam the formula page was missing formulas as well. Take someone else if you want a good grade.

His formula sheet for exams is garbage, gives basically no layout to what will be on the exams, and lectures are entirely theory while exams/homework are just straight computation. You honestly are just going to have to teach yourself the entire class.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are not related to test and homework content at all. Be prepared to study heavily outside of class. Textbook has a lot of content, and it is difficult to study for the exam without study a lot of unnecessary content.

reviews.comment: Terrible. Homework is easy but has almost no correlation to the exams and the formula sheet will not help in the slightest. It's about as hard as winning the lottery to have the exam questions be like what you studied.
reviews.ratingTags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't let his old reviews fool you... Every time I step into this lecture, I am bored out of my mind and learn nothing. Take Hans Schuessler instead.

reviews.comment: Do not take if you actually want to learn. As stated before, HUGE disconnect between lecture and exams/homework. If you can push this class back to avoid him, I would say it 100% worth it.

reviews.comment: Exams are really tough, lectures were unclear and he wasn't accessible outside the class.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: As long as you do well on one of the exams (in the B-curve range) and get high marks on the homeworks you should be able to get through this class with a B.

reviews.comment: The only thing I learned in this class was how to pray. Just spent the entire class reading out of the textbook, which didn't even teach.

reviews.comment: Just terrible. Overpriced book and lazy lectures. Do yourself a favor and switch to computer engineering to dodge this guy.

reviews.comment: Tenzier makes this class so much harder than it needs to be. Studying for his exams is very difficult, so my suggestion is to get past exams. reviews.comment: Teizer teaches by reading out of the book. The book does not convey the material in an understandable way, so Teizer does not teach the content in an understandable way. reviews.comment: Bro does not like to work out any problems, rather just read out of a textbook. Textbook is long, problems from the textbook are not explained, so you have to use third-party websites to get any real answers. good luck.
reviews.ratingTags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Homework will help, but make sure to do reviews. He is difficult to understand and not clear on explaining some topics. I read and did examples in the book and still was confused. The final is extremely difficult. Make sure to study and do reviews and extra practice.

reviews.comment: Teaches by reading out of textbook, tests are quite difficult and his suggestions for studying are not great. The textbook isn't very good either, so good luck.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: You will have to teach yourself as he does not do example problems in class. My advice is to do textbook problems in the back of the chapter and redo homework problems for exam prep. Most questions on the exams were very similar to those on the homework, so if you can do the homework (and actually understand what you're doing), you'll be fine.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read

reviews.comment: If you pay attention in his lectures, you'll be fine, but as soon as you zone out once, you're basically screwed. The textbook is super helpful and is essentially the only way I learned anything in this course. Tests are very difficult and require solving the textbook examples to succeed, don't leave studying for this class until the last minute.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Teizer is an excellent lecturer who eloquently explains complex physics concepts and connects them to the real world with entertaining demonstrations. He is easily accessible and gives lenient curves, but there is a disconnect between the theory-heavy lectures and the math-heavy exams and HW, so the textbook is important if you want to do well.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Respected--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There was a big disconnect between exams and homeworks and classroom material taught. It was hard to understand what was expected to do well. If you are a good textbook learner, this class is great. If you need an actual professor teaching, look elsewhere.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures were copy and pasted directly from the textbook and he just read from them. His explanations and examples were all also based from the textbook and there was little to no guidance on how tests would be formed. He isn't a good professor unless you want an audiobook instead of having to read a textbook.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Teizer for PHYS 206 and 222. He was alright both times. Not anything special, but there are definitely worse professors out there for physics courses. I would take again simply because I know what to expect from him.
reviews.ratingTags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Teizer is honestly a very competent professor, but his lectures are heavy on theory and almost no math which is 90% of HW/ exams. Modern physics is already complicated as it is and lectures don't help, so you're forced to learn from the textbook. Personally, I can't learn by reading textbooks so I really suffered as a result.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His way of teaching did not stick to me and most students. He never went through example problems, only theory, which makes a class like this more tough. The tests were also pretty unpredictable (sometimes difficult, sometimes easy). If you have him, you're going to be doing a LOT of self-teaching.

Professor Teizer is well versed in physics. He makes his class entertaining and does experiments to demonstrate what he is saying. You must study the textbook, but his class is enjoyable and the way he grades exam is very fair. He is a good and fair professor, and his class gives you good knowledge about what you are going to be applying in the HWs
reviews.ratingTags: Inspirational--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Teizer does not go through any examples or practical applications of the equations he shows in class. The lectures are reserved only to conceptual topics, which is not what is evaluated on the exams. There is a great disconnect between the lecture and the exams/homework. Physics should be taught by going through examples and problems.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not the worst but also not the best. The lectures are theory based and he doesn't work out problems. Huge disconnect between class and homework/exams. If you don't study the textbook questions for exams, you won't do well. Pop quizzes every once in a while but they are easy and based off reading. Responds fast to emails and fast test turnaround.

PHYS222 is already a mess of a class, but with his purely theory based lectures, homeworks are 2/3rds of the time impossible, and exams are pretty rough. The amount of time that would be required to truly understand this course's material for exams is unreasonably long. Only saving grace is good partial credit on the exams and a heavy curve.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Physics is tough at A&M but Dr. Teizer did a good job teaching. He goes over some of the harder problems from the textbook in class. There is not enough time to cover everything you need to know during class time so you have to do some on your own. Homework can be time consuming but is useful for the tests. Odd but good grading system!
reviews.ratingTags: Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Teizer is a good professor, but if you can avoid taking Mechanical Physics at A&M, do it at all costs. The tests are very difficult, and Dr. Teizer goes over problems almost exclusively from the textbook. He's a very sweet and personable guy, but sometimes his in-depth explanations may go over your head if you're not a physics lover.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Literally any prof you get for phys 206 is going to be tough because it's not an easy subject. Teizer was a good prof, and I really like how the physics department does the learning objectives approach. He always went over tough questions during lecture, so be sure to watch the prelectures beforehand.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Solid prof; teaching style is very theory heavy which could be a turn off for some but he does work out a few problems every lecture; knowledgeable and easy to approach and talk to

Dr. Teizer is one of the best STEM professors I have ever had, full stop. His accent is easy to understand, and he is a fantastic lecturer. The homework is a pain and there is a LOT of calculations, but this is PHYS at Texas A&M. I honestly wish I had more profs like him earlier in college, I would've done so much better.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Physics at A&M are no joke. This class made Calc 2 seem like a cake walk. You move quick and the material is brushed over. There is simply not enough time for him to teach you everything, you must learn to learn on your own. Great prof though.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were fairly standard stuff, going through the theory. Not too many examples in class, but that's what recitation is for, so you should honestly be getting enough examples in there. Exams were fairly in line, if not easier, than the homework, though they have an unsual (but good) grading system. I enjoyed his lectures a decent amount.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Teizer is a very smart guy who loves physics and tries to make it enjoyable for the class. He's very funny, would often show us funny videos and get our feedback in his teaching. His accent is interesting but easy to understand. Physics is hard but I would take Dr. Teizer again, he has some tricks for solvinf specific Physics problems.
reviews.ratingTags: Test heavy--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Teizer is extremely intelligent on the subject matter, but is not "in tune" with normal teaching methods. Lectures are just that: lectures. We did less than 5 example problems throughout the semester, and were expected to learn how to do the problems via just the homework. Tests averages were 54, 55, and 61 (MT, MT, final). I got a B with a 65.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Although Dr. Teizer is very knowledgeable about Physics and he's good with returning exams in a timely manner, I wouldn't recommend him for this class. He focuses a ton on theory, so when tests come around, you really have to work to fill the gap between theory and application. Unless you're a genius, outside tutoring's required if you want an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Worst explanations but the most entertaining experiments. If you like magic shows, go for it. If u care about your grade and want to understand the material, he is just gonna confuse you. Also he is very slow and u will have a good sleep :)
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Teizer was a fantastic lecturer. It is clear he knows his stuff well, and he can communicate it very well for a lecture hall of over 100 people.  He has a slight accent that does not hinder ability to understand what he's saying at all.  The examples he does in class comes from the book. I suck at physics so don't let my C stop you from getting him
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Teizer is a good professor. His lectures are pretty clear, but he doesn't do many examples. He occasionally plays funny gifs to drive in content, and wants to see you succeed. He's not a professor that will become your best friend, but is helpful if you go to his office. In general, 218 is just really hard though.

Light accent. He was very inspirational to me. He would give little background history lessons about important people in physics like Newton and Kepler. He would make the class funny, by showing funny videos and such. His lectures are a little broad, however he does go over problems in class, and gives you plenty of opportunity to ask questions.

From Germany so a light accent but not hard to understand at all. Has some funny moments in lecture but overall is vague so reading suplement materials like the textbook will be very helpful for the class. Tough common tests however that, during my year, he did not write.
